Infrastructure Update

TurboFlow Adopts Chainlink for XAU, BTC, and ETH Continuous Prediction Markets

TurboFlow and Chainlink announced that TurboFlow had adopted Chainlink to support new continuous prediction markets for XAU, BTC, and ETH. The official posts confirm the integration and named markets without identifying a specific Chainlink service or deployment configuration.

Published June 11, 2026 Updated August 12, 2026 By TurboFlow

Source: X

Source content

This section preserves the source's facts, attribution, and narrative order. It is a faithful editorial adaptation, not a verbatim reproduction.

On June 11, 2026, TurboFlow said on its official X account that, with Chainlink, it was enabling fast, accurate, and continuous prediction markets intended for global retail participation.

Chainlink then confirmed through its official X account that TurboFlow had adopted Chainlink to power new continuous prediction markets for XAU, BTC, and ETH.

The two official posts confirm TurboFlow's adoption of Chainlink and name XAU, BTC, and ETH as the announced markets.

Summary

  • IntegrationTurboFlow adopted Chainlink.
  • Market formatThe announcement uses the term continuous prediction markets.
  • Named marketsXAU, BTC, and ETH.

Frequently asked questions

What did TurboFlow and Chainlink announce?

They announced that TurboFlow had adopted Chainlink to support new continuous prediction markets.

When was the Chainlink integration announced?

TurboFlow and Chainlink published their official X posts on June 11, 2026.

Which markets were named in the announcement?

Chainlink's official post named XAU, BTC, and ETH.

Which Chainlink service did TurboFlow adopt?

The two official posts do not identify a specific Chainlink service, feed, or deployment configuration.

Did the announcement explicitly name TurboFlow Event Contracts?

No. Both posts use the term continuous prediction markets; neither post explicitly names Event Contracts.

The announcement concerns infrastructure support and does not guarantee price accuracy, uninterrupted operation, execution quality, or trading outcomes. Event Contracts are short-duration products, and an incorrect direction can result in loss of the stake.
